description: Portable deterministic security policy for AI Engineering Workflow across all runtimes
invariants: Zero Secret Exposure: Never log, commit, or return secrets, keys, or credentials.
Deterministic Boundaries: Never treat prompt instructions alone as the sole security barrier.
Least Privilege: Limit tool permissions to minimum required operational scope.
Explicit Approval: High-blast-radius or irreversible actions require explicit user authorization.

blockedOperations.reason: Root or drive directory deletion is strictly blocked
Disk format commands are strictly blocked
Raw database drop operations are strictly blocked outside controlled migrations
Git force push to remote branches is strictly blocked
Indiscriminate deletion of untracked files without confirmation is blocked
Direct console display of secret and credential files is blocked

approvalRequiredOperations.reason: Hard git reset discards uncommitted work and requires explicit approval
Package publishing impacts external registries and requires explicit approval
Docker prune clears local containers/images and requires explicit approval
Production cloud infrastructure deployment requires explicit approval

redactionRules: JWT secrets, private keys, database passwords, and API tokens must never appear in commit messages, logs, or agent conversation history.

cursor.mechanism: Native command approval dialogs and terminal confirmation
cursor.enforcer: Runtime approval controls + pre-execution policy checks

vscode.mechanism: GitHub Copilot terminal confirmation & workspace trust
vscode.enforcer: Runtime approval controls + pre-execution policy checks

codex.mechanism: OpenAI Codex CLI execution sandboxing & approval flags
codex.enforcer: Codex sandbox policy + pre-execution policy checks

claude-code.mechanism: Claude Code command permissions & interactive confirmation
claude-code.enforcer: Runtime permission checks + pre-execution policy checks

gemini-cli.mechanism: Gemini CLI execution approval and tool confirmation

fallbackBehavior: When running in a runtime lacking deterministic pre-tool hooks, the agent must check proposed commands against this policy before execution, refusing blocked commands and explicitly requesting user confirmation for approval-required operations.
